abstract:
Abstract
The Dorabella cipher is an encrypted note writ-
ten by English composer Edward Elgar, which
has defied decipherment attempts for more than
a century. While most proposed solutions are
English texts, we investigate the hypothesis that
Dorabella represents enciphered music. We
weigh the evidence for and against the hypoth-
esis, devise a simplified music notation, and
attempt to reconstruct a melody from the ci-
pher. Our tools are n-gram models of music
which we validate on existing music corpora
enciphered using monoalphabetic substitution.
By applying our methods to Dorabella, we pro-
duce a decipherment with musical qualities,
which is then transformed via artful composi-
tion into a listenable melody. Far from arguing
that the end result represents the only true solu-
tion, we instead frame the process of decipher-
ment as part of the composition process.

Conclusions
Although we do not claim to have solved the mys-
tery of Dorabella, our process produced a listenable
melody, which opens up interesting avenues of in-
vestigation. In the future, we plan to experiment
with different corpora and musical attributes, such
as rhythm only. Our approach represents a creative
way to generate new forms of musical melodies.
What seems certain is that Elgar’s intention to con-
found left us with a tantalizing riddle that invites
further speculation in the future.
